tax_year: FY 2026-27 (Tax Year 2026-27; unchanged from FY 2025-26 / AY 2026-27)
regime: new (section 202 of the Income-tax Act 2025; formerly section 115BAC of the 1961 Act)
source: Income tax: Income Tax Department (incometaxindia.gov.in) AY 2026-27 rate table; Finance Act 2025 (slabs/SD/rebate) and Finance Act 2026 / Budget 2026, which made NO change to the new-regime slab rates, the Rs 75,000 standard deduction, or the section 87A rebate (Rs 60,000 up to Rs 12 L) -- and the Income-tax Act 2025 (Act 30 of 2025, in force from 1 Apr 2026) carries the same amounts over (section 202; rebate renumbered to section 156). ESI: ESIC (esic.gov.in), employee 0.75% / employer 3.25% on gross wages up to Rs 21,000/month (Rs 25,000 for persons with disability). Professional Tax: Maharashtra State Tax on Professions Act (employee-side monthly slab).
notes: Income-tax figures are the new regime for FY 2026-27 (Tax Year 2026-27), verified unchanged from FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27): slabs Rs 4/8/12/16/20/24 L @ 5/10/15/20/25/30%, Rs 75,000 standard deduction, section 87A rebate Rs 60,000 up to Rs 12 L with marginal relief, 4% health & education cess. Budget 2026 left these unchanged, so the same numbers apply to both years; under the Income-tax Act 2025 (from 1 Apr 2026) they are renumbered (115BAC -> 202, 87A -> 156). EPF modelled at the statutory Rs 15,000/month wage ceiling (Rs 1,80,000/year) at 12% employee and employer, applied to gross because Basic+DA is not available here. Statutory deductions include ESI (0.75% employee / 3.25% employer on gross up to Rs 21,000/month; nil above) and Maharashtra Professional Tax (Rs 0 up to Rs 7,500, Rs 175/month up to Rs 10,000, Rs 200/month above, capped Rs 2,500/year). Professional Tax is state-specific: the Maharashtra slab is the default example; other states differ and stock Frappe HR only categorises PT (no slab computation). New regime assumed; old-regime deductions (80C, HRA, etc.) are not modelled. Illustrative until an accountant reviews it.
